item.title: What Every Music Company Made in Q2 2026 (Updating)
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the latest news from the music industry. I'm your host, and today we're talking about the recent earnings reports from music companies. Let's take a look at the numbers.
[Soft music transitions in the background]
Host: It's been a strong few weeks for music companies, with around a dozen publicly traded firms reporting their earnings. And the early results are in: consumers are still spending on music. From major labels to music streamers, satellite radio to live events, the numbers are looking good.
For example, Universal Music Group and Sony Music have both reported solid results, with Sony Music seeing a 20% surge in revenue year-over-year. And in Korea, HYBE is riding high on the success of K-pop supergroup BTS' world tour and album sales.
But it's not just the labels that are doing well. Live Nation has also seen a significant increase in quarterly revenue, despite competition from FIFA World Cup games. And Sphere Entertainment has reported a revenue increase from showings of The Wizard of Oz, although they did suffer an overall operating loss.
[Music transitions to a slightly different tone]
Host: Satellite radio giant SiriusXM Holdings is also finding its footing, thanks to low-cost companion plans and premium channels featuring big names like Morgan Wallen and Green Day. And on the streaming front, Deezer has reported a slight increase in revenue and adjusted gross profit.
[Music transitions back to the intro tone]
Host: We're not done yet, though. Spotify and Warner Music Group are still set to report their earnings, on August 4th and 6th respectively. We'll be keeping an eye on those results and bringing you updates as earnings season progresses.
[Outro music plays]
Host: That's all for today. Thanks for tuning in to our podcast, and we'll catch you on the next one.
